findings.issue: Italian Front had no position between 23 Oct and 1 Nov 1917, so the loss of Cividale (27 Oct) and Udine (28 Oct) never appeared, and the Austro-German occupation of Friuli only faded in after 1 Nov. Added the West Point 28 Oct line (Mt Maggiore-Tarcento-Udine) and occupation keys from 24 Oct.

source.title: USMA West Point Atlas of the Great War, plate 15: Battle of Caporetto, situation 24 Oct and operations to 12 Nov 1917 (Wikimedia Commons)

findings.issue: Tagliamento position (1 Nov) left the Carnic sector west of Tolmezzo; plate 15 shows the 1 Nov line still on the Carnic crest down to Moggio, then along the Tagliamento by Cornino and Latisana. Redrawn, and held to 3 Nov (Cornino bridge forced 3 Nov; retreat to the Piave ordered after Codroipo fell 4 Nov).

Only two keys (1 Nov, 12 Nov) for the retreat Tagliamento -> Piave; added the Livenza line of 6 Nov and the Piave/Grappa line on 10 Nov (the Caporetto article: position on the Piave established by 10 Nov).

The 1914-border base map paints the Italian-held Isonzo strip (Gorizia, Bainsizza, Plezzo/Caporetto bank, Cortina) as Austro-Hungarian before the battle, so the breakthrough showed no lost ground there. New occupation 'Italian-held ground beyond the 1914 border and on the Grappa-Piave line' (side 0) follows every Italian Front key; it only draws on enemy ground.

source.title: USMA West Point Atlas of the Great War, plate 15: Battle of Caporetto, situation 24 Oct and operations to 12 Nov 1917 (Wikimedia Commons)

findings.issue: Text said the army held on the Piave 'with British and French help'; plate 15 notes the six Franco-British divisions arriving in November played a minor role in the defence of the Piave line. Text now: Udine 28 Oct, Tagliamento, Piave and Monte Grappa held from about 10 Nov, Allied divisions arrived to reinforce.

source.title: USMA West Point Atlas of the Great War, plate 15: Battle of Caporetto, situation 24 Oct and operations to 12 Nov 1917 (Wikimedia Commons)

findings.issue: Occupation 'Austro-German-occupied north-east Italy (after Caporetto)' now also carries the 1916 Asiago-plateau gains (keys from 14 May 1916, built from the same front lines), so that ground does not pop in with Caporetto. The name could not be changed through the patch format.

source.title: USMA West Point Atlas of the Great War, plate 15: Battle of Caporetto, situation 24 Oct and operations to 12 Nov 1917 (Wikimedia Commons)

findings.issue: The 1918 base map paints Monte Grappa, the Montello and Bassano as Austro-Hungarian all year; the Italian-held ring above restores the Grappa-Piave strip to Italy.

source.title: USMA West Point Atlas of the Great War, plate 15: Battle of Caporetto, situation 24 Oct and operations to 12 Nov 1917 (Wikimedia Commons)

findings.issue: Austria-Hungary leaves the sides on 3 Nov 1918 (toDate), so the old 'north-east Italy' occupation (side 1, keys to 31 Oct, no end) would suddenly draw red over all of Friuli and Veneto from 3 Nov, i.e. after the Italian victory. Removed its 1918 keys and set end 1918-10-14 (fully faded before 3 Nov; in 1918 the base map already shows that ground as Austro-Hungarian).

Vittorio Veneto had keys only on 23 Oct, 31 Oct and 4 Nov: no Piave bridgeheads, no Vittorio Veneto (30 Oct), Belluno (1 Nov), Trento, Udine or Trieste (3 Nov); the 4 Nov line stopped at the Tagliamento and the recovered ground was never shown. Added keys 28 Oct, 30 Oct, 1 Nov, 3 Nov and a 4 Nov line through Cles/Dimaro, north of Trento, Levico, Tolmezzo, Cividale, Cormons and Aquileia (cavalry positions at the 15:00 ceasefire); the Italian-held ring covers the advance plus a coastal tongue for the Trieste landing of 3 Nov.

Italian Front (last key 4 Nov) held on screen until the German armistice of 11 Nov. Re-issued the front with end 1918-11-04 (Villa Giusti ceasefire 15:00 4 Nov). Done via new_fronts because apply_review.py ignores 'end' on a front patch.

Vittorio Veneto arrow started on 24 Oct and ran east of the Piave; the river was crossed on 27 Oct. Arrow now starts 27 Oct at the Montello crossing and runs via Vittorio Veneto towards the Tagliamento.

The 1917 base map paints Gaza and Beersheba as British (British Africa) all year, so both appeared Allied before 31 Oct / 7 Nov, and the Ottoman line had no ground behind it. New occupation 'Ottoman-held Palestine, Transjordan and Syria (1917-1918)' (side 1) covers the Ottoman side of each front position (only draws on Allied ground).

source.title: USMA West Point Atlas, Palestine 1917: Third Battle of Gaza and capture of Jerusalem (Wikimedia Commons)

findings.issue: Front jumped from the Gaza-Beersheba line (30 Oct) straight to Jaffa (16 Nov): Beersheba (31 Oct), Hareira-Sheria (6 Nov), Gaza (7 Nov) and Junction Station (14 Nov) never appeared. Added keys 30 Oct (line south of Beersheba), 1 Nov, 6 Nov, 7 Nov, 14 Nov.

No key between 16 Nov and 30 Dec, so Jerusalem only came into British ground through interpolation weeks late and Nebi Samwil (21-24 Nov) was missing. Added 24 Nov and 9 Dec (city surrendered 9 Dec, Allenby's entry 11 Dec) keys; 30 Dec line moved north of Bireh and of the Auja (crossing 21-22 Dec) per the West Point 30 Dec line.

source.title: USMA West Point Atlas, Palestine 1917: Third Battle of Gaza and capture of Jerusalem (Wikimedia Commons)

findings.issue: Allenby arrow reached Beersheba only after ~10 days of animation and bypassed the coastal advance. Path now starts south-west of Beersheba; new arrow 'XXI Corps takes Gaza and advances to Jaffa' (1-16 Nov) added to the chapter.

The 1918 base map paints all of Palestine, Transjordan and Syria British/Hejazi from 1 Jan 1918, so before Megiddo the Ottoman-held north (Nablus, Damascus, Aleppo) looked Allied and the breakthrough showed no ground changing hands. The Ottoman-held ring above follows the front to 30 Oct and ends with Mudros (only a thin sliver north of the Aleppo line at the end, so nothing lingers on Turkish soil).

source.title: USMA West Point Atlas, plate 50: Battle of Megiddo, 19-25 Sep 1918, and pursuit to Damascus (Wikimedia Commons)

findings.issue: Palestine front jumped 18 Sep -> 1 Oct -> 30 Oct: no Tulkarm/Afula/Nazareth (19-20 Sep), Nablus (21 Sep), Haifa/Es Salt (23 Sep), Amman/Samakh (25 Sep), Deraa (27 Sep); Aleppo (25/26 Oct) was only reached by interpolation on 30 Oct and Beirut (8 Oct), Homs (16 Oct), Hama (c. 20 Oct) were absent. Added keys 20, 22, 25, 28 Sep and 8, 16, 21, 26 Oct (West Point plate 50 lines of 20 and 25 Sep), plus arrow 'Pursuit from Damascus to Aleppo'. The 30 Oct line is trimmed at 37.6E so British ground does not spill onto Turkish soil after the armistice.

Sinai and Palestine Front and Mesopotamian Front (last keys 30 Oct) stayed on screen until 11 Nov although the Mudros armistice took effect at noon on 31 Oct. Both re-issued with end 1918-10-31 via new_fronts. (Mosul was occupied on 1-2 Nov after the armistice and is deliberately not drawn as a front move.)

Macedonian front had no position between 14 and 24 Sep, so the Dobro Pole breach (15 Sep; 25 km wide and 7 km deep by 16 Sep) did not appear. Added a 17 Sep key with the breach and matching Serbian-occupation keys on 17 and 24 Sep.
On 29 Sep Skopje sat exactly on the edge of the Central Powers occupation of Serbia; moved the 29 Sep front and occupation edge a few km north (French troops entered Skopje 11:00 on 29 Sep).

'Central Powers-occupied Serbia and Montenegro' had no end, so a strip of western Serbia stayed Central Powers-held until 11 Nov although Belgrade was retaken on 1 Nov and Austria-Hungary's armistice took effect on 4 Nov. Added a 4 Nov key shrinking it to a sliver on the Drina and end 1918-11-04. (This occupation's earlier keys belong to the Serbia reviewer; only 1918 keys were touched, to keep it continuous with the Macedonian front.)

source.title: Wikipedia: Liberation of Serbia, Albania and Montenegro (1918)

findings.issue: The Macedonian front's Drina-Sava segment (facing Austria-Hungary) stayed drawn until 11 Nov. Added a 4 Nov key that leaves only the Danube line Belgrade-Iron Gates (Franchet d'Esperey's army crossed the Danube on 10 Nov). A clean end for this shared front would need 'end' support for fronts in apply_review.py.

source.title: Wikipedia: Liberation of Serbia, Albania and Montenegro (1918)

findings.issue: Not fixed (outside the patch format): no battle markers for Beersheba/Third Gaza, Jerusalem, Dobro Pole or Sharqat (the patch cannot add battles); the per-year base-map snapshots themselves (1917/1918 Palestine, 1918 Veneto) are wrong and are corrected here only by occupation overlays.

source.title: USMA West Point Atlas, plate 50: Battle of Megiddo, 19-25 Sep 1918, and pursuit to Damascus (Wikimedia Commons)

findings.issue: Not fixed: Mesopotamian 31 May 1918 key puts the Tigris end at Fat-ha (35.05N), c. 20 km north of the British line near Tikrit; Kirkuk (taken 7 May 1918, evacuated after 18 days, retaken 25/26 Oct) is not drawn. Outside all chapter areas, left for a later pass. The British advance up the Tigris (from 23 Oct) and Ottoman surrender at Sharqat (30 Oct) match the 30 Oct key.

caporetto.text: After eleven costly battles on the Isonzo, Austro-German forces broke through at Caporetto on 24 October 1917 and took Udine on the 28th. The Italian army fell back to the Tagliamento and then more than 100 km to the Piave river and Monte Grappa, where it held from about 10 November; British and French divisions arrived to reinforce it.
